review.headline: A dominant middlegame and winning conversion cut short by the clock

sections.text: You navigated the opening cleanly against White's passive setup, securing the bishop pair with 10...Nxg3. You faced a brief stumble with 12...c5, which handed White an initiative, followed by 13...b6. However, White immediately faltered with 14.h4, allowing you to lock down the kingside with the strong push 14...g4! and keep White's pieces cramped.

Once White misplayed with 16.Nd5, you seized total control of the board. You opened lines on the queenside with 17...a6 and 18...axb5, quickly activating your rooks and queen. Your heavy pieces dominated the a-file while White's king remained stranded in the center.

From there, your execution was ruthless. You removed White's advanced knight with 24...Bxd5, traded down cleanly on a2, and scooped up pawns with 28...Rxf5 and 32...Rxg2. After 33...Bh6+ you were up four pawns and completely winning, but sadly ran out of time.

review.turning_point: White's 14.h4 allowed your powerful 14...g4 push, burying White's knight and giving you full control over the pace of the game.
review.focus: Be careful with flank pawn advances like 12...c5 that weaken your central structure when central breaks like 12...d5 are available.
